<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>Detects the specific 4-bit binary sequence '1001' using a finite state machine (FSM).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">Reset signal to initialize the state machine.</input>
        <input id="data_in">1-bit binary input signal for the bitstream being fed into the sequence detector.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">1-bit output signal indicating whether the specific sequence has been detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Waiting for the start of the sequence.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">First bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">Second bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">Third bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">Fourth and final bit of the desired sequence is detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="next_state">Next state for the state machine.</signal>
        
        <always_comb>
            case(state)
                IDLE: next_state = data_in ? S1 : IDLE;
                S1: next_state = ~data_in ? S2 : IDLE;
                S2: next_state = ~data_in ? S3 : IDLE;
                S3: next_state = data_in ? S4 : IDLE;
                S4: next_state = data_in ? IDLE : S1;
                default: next_state = IDLE;
            endcase
        </always_comb>
    </logic_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state">State variable for the state machine.</reg>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or posedge reset_n) begin
            if (reset_n)
                state <= IDLE;
            else
                state <= next_state;
        end
        
        <assign sequence_detected = (state == S4);
    </logic_description>
</module>
